rationale: Guidance states non-human entities be considered differently from user-based identities at registration; reaches the machine case explicitly.
Requires least privilege for users (or processes acting on behalf of users); the parenthetical extends the principle to non-human processes.
Requires unique identification and authentication of natural persons and systems, but the operative account-assignment duty in Art. 20(2)(a) is staff-scoped, so not C.
Mandates need-to-know, need-to-use and least privilege including for remote and emergency access.
Adversarial read of both articles returns nothing governing delegated authority or the transfer of access rights between principals.
IA-9 is the nearest control but governs service authentication rather than delegation, and it is allocated to no baseline in any of the four OSCAL profiles.
Full-text search of the consolidated statute returns no machine identity, service account, API or AI agent; BSI guidance frames account management around Benutzende.
No Annex A category corresponds to access control, credentials or identity; the standard defers information-security controls to ISO/IEC 27001 by design.
Names the autonomy boundary explicitly, but uses should, prescribes only a major consideration, sits in an overview clause, and the document states no requirements at all.
Governs what happens prior to issuing system credentials, which presupposes the credential is issued through the front door.
